fact: A June 2026 Addis Ababa workshop co-hosted by the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research and the Agricultural Transformation Institute trained 50+ staff from seven countries including Ethiopia on the satellite-based CropWatch and ETWatch platforms for crop area, yield and evapotranspiration mapping, per AIRCAS.

FAO's EOSTAT project, with the Ethiopian Statistics Service, trained national experts in February 2025 in Adama and ran a pilot wheat yield study in Arsi Zone using DSSAT with Earth observation data and the GCVI vegetation index.

The Ministry of Agriculture's agri data hub lists EthioSIS soil-nutrient layers that MoA-ATI generated using field-lab data and satellite data covariates in machine learning models, created October 2024 and updated 24 March 2026.

The Agricultural Transformation Institute, WFP and Pula Advisors ran an area-yield index insurance scheme based on remotely sensed rainfall estimates that reached 122,000 smallholder farmers in Amhara in Meher 2023, with 39 million birr paid to 52,000 farmers.

The Ethiopian Meteorology Institute's satellite bulletin for 21-30 September 2026 analyses vegetation greenness from METEOSAT products and TAMSAT rainfall estimates, finding sparse to bare vegetation in Afar, Somali and southern Oromia.
The Ethiopian Meteorology Institute publishes its satellite bulletin per dekad, the issue covering the third dekad (21-30) of September 2026.

FAO says 30 staff of regional agriculture and irrigation bureaus, the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research and the Ministry of Agriculture were trained in crop mapping from satellite imagery using Google Earth Engine, delivered by trained trainers from Addis Ababa Institute of Technology, the Ministry and EIAR.
